description: The figure presents an error-analysis comparison between two models using two side-by-side pie charts, with the Vanilla model on the left and the HCL model on the right, each partitioning outcomes into four categories. In both charts, there are four slices corresponding to the legend at the top: “Atomic Skill Fail” (dark teal), “Correct” (medium blue-teal), “Reason Error” (light blue-gray), and “Question Misunderstood” (very light gray/near-white). The Vanilla model pie shows Atomic Skill Fail at approximately 68.0%, Correct at 12.0%, Reason Error at 12.0%, and Question Misunderstood at 8.0%, with percentage labels printed inside each slice. The HCL model pie shows Correct at approximately 55.0%, Reason Error at 21.0%, Question Misunderstood at 14.0%, and Atomic Skill Fail at 10.0%, also with percentage labels inside the slices. A shared legend is present, and neither pie appears to use exploded/offset slices or other visual emphasis; the slice arrangement appears to place the largest segment prominently but is not strictly ordered around the circle.
